dimension_justifications.soundness: The definitions, scope boundaries, and distinction between selection stability and null calibration are unusually careful. However, every central quantitative claim is marked source_reported/cannot_verify_locally, the event streams and analysis code are absent, the private checkpoint is not equivalent to the public release, the original gate was anti-conservative, and the decisive structured-null, dual-recorder, and factorial interventions were not run. The core is plausible but has substantive verification and identification gaps.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The manuscript is readable, anonymous, within the nine-page main-text limit, explicit about limitations, and includes reproducibility and AI-use disclosures. The central narrative is nevertheless burdened by extensive terminology, repeated caveats and tables, large unused page regions, and novelty comparisons relegated to dense appendix matrices whose support cannot be checked.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The paper offers a precise cautionary case study about schedule-aligned measurement artifacts and a useful reachability-versus-magnitude reporting distinction. Its empirical scope is one private checkpoint, one task, one recorder family, and a selector whose alignment with imposed block boundaries may be expected from the measurement construction. No model mechanism, downstream decision improvement, cross-recorder effect, or generality is established, and priority over the closest literature cannot be verified from the supplied citation record.

paper_summary: The paper studies identity-lock-time periodicity measured by an active-block recorder for a blockwise diffusion language model. It varies block length together with the required per-block step allocation and reports that a registered min-max selector and a rank-sum comparison select the configured length in five arms, including two non-nested canvas-96 probes. It carefully limits the result to recorder-observable selection stability, not null-calibrated detection or model-mechanism attribution, and recommends separating estimator reachability from event-derived magnitude.
strongest_verified_contribution: Within the frozen snapshot, the strongest defensible contribution is the explicit formal separation between what boundary-set algebra makes reachable before observing data and what measured magnitudes establish afterward, together with unusually transparent disclosure of the composite intervention, post-treatment scope amendment, failed original calibration gate, and recorder-relative claim boundary. The five-arm numerical findings themselves remain source-reported and cannot_verify from the supplied artifacts.
strengths: Sections 2 and 3 distinguish bootstrap stability from false-positive control and avoid interpreting 0/2000 misses as calibrated detection.
The manuscript openly reports the post-treatment withdrawal of the model-intrinsic branch, the reused L32 development control, the marginal L24 result, and the single-boundary L48 result.
The non-power-of-two probes, rank-sum comparison, rank-transform check, and narrow spectral diagnostic are sensible attempts to challenge a purely nested-candidate explanation.
The paper does not overstate its result as a model mechanism and explicitly identifies the missing dual-recorder, factorial-allocation, and cross-model tests.
Anonymity, main-text page limit, ethics screening information, reproducibility boundary, and AI-assisted preparation disclosure are present.
questions: Which primary papers are genuinely closest on position-resolved commit or lock timing under blockwise active observation, and what exact passages support every contrast in Tables 13 and 14?
What practical scientific conclusion or downstream diagnostic decision would be wrong without the proposed two-layer reporting rule and corrected after applying it?
On identical generated trajectories, does a full-canvas or passive recorder remove or materially alter the reported periodicity relative to the active-block recorder?
Can partition and per-block allocation be varied independently enough to determine which component drives boundary location and magnitude?
Can the anonymized event streams and analysis programs be supplied so that Tables 2 through 7 and the bootstrap readouts can be independently rebuilt?

issues.location: Section 5, pages 8-9; Appendix A.9, Tables 13-14, pages 16-17; literature/citation_lock.json
issues.observed_evidence: The manuscript presents row-wise nearest-work contrasts and states that the cited evidence does not establish the same active-block-recorder intervention. The supplied citation lock is explicitly partial and contains only one completed check; it does not provide primary-source support for the local claims in Tables 13 and 14. Consequently, the asserted closest-work distinctions are cannot_verify rather than demonstrated false.
issues.why_it_matters: The empirical contribution is narrow, so acceptance depends heavily on establishing that the exact measurement problem and intervention have not already been analyzed. Without auditable closest-work support, the contribution score cannot exceed narrow or incremental.
issues.required_fix: Verify every nearest-work row and every absence-style contrast against the cited primary source, add the most directly relevant work on blockwise decoding diagnostics and schedule-induced measurement artifacts, and place a concise supported closest-work comparison in the main text.
issues.verification_test: An independent reader can trace each substantive Table 13-14 contrast to a section, equation, figure, or experiment in the primary paper, and a targeted literature audit finds no omitted work evaluating the same recorder-window and block-length intervention.
issues.evidence_needed: A complete citation lock with verified metadata and local-support records for every novelty-bearing sentence and table row, plus a closest-work search log covering active-block recording, token commitment or lock time, schedule periodicity, and instrumentation confounds.

issues.location: Abstract and contribution paragraph on pages 1-2; Equation 2 and Sections 2-3.2 on pages 3-8; Appendix A.4 and A.6 on pages 14-15
issues.observed_evidence: The active recorder exposes only the current block, candidate boundaries are defined directly from period P, and the treatment changes the configured block partition. The paper itself proves P*=L only for strictly L-supported profiles and labels the main finding descriptive. The proposed canon largely instantiates established construct-validity principles: record the intervention, calibrate the observation window, and separate design reachability from empirical magnitude.
issues.why_it_matters: As presented, the result risks being an expected consequence of the instrument and selector rather than substantial new knowledge about diffusion language models or measurement methodology. The manuscript does not demonstrate a previously consequential wrong inference, a corrected downstream decision, or broad applicability.
issues.required_fix: Identify a concrete prior diagnostic inference that this effect changes, evaluate the corrected protocol against that inference, and either demonstrate generality across an independent model or schedule or explicitly reposition the work as a narrowly scoped negative measurement case study with correspondingly modest novelty claims.
issues.verification_test: A preregistered application shows that using the uncalibrated versus calibrated diagnostic changes a scientifically meaningful conclusion on held-out data, or replicated independent settings show the same failure mode while the literature audit establishes that this diagnostic correction is distinct.
issues.evidence_needed: A decision-relevance experiment and at least one independent model, sampler, schedule, or recorder setting, together with verified closest-work comparisons.

issues.location: Table 1 and matched-intervention discussion on pages 3-4; Limitations on page 8; evidence/experiment_registry.json entries A31-X3 and A31-X4
issues.observed_evidence: Block partition and required per-block allocation change together, and no identical-trajectory dual active/full-canvas recorder comparison was run. The registry marks both the partition-by-allocation factorial and dual-recorder experiment as not_run. The manuscript appropriately declines a mechanism claim, but its recorder-confound motivation is therefore not causally isolated.
issues.why_it_matters: Without isolating allocation, partition, and observation-window effects, the work establishes only association with a composite schedule. That boundary substantially limits both technical interpretation and the novelty of the reporting recommendation.
issues.required_fix: Run the smallest factorial intervention that varies partition and allocation independently where feasible, and log identical trajectories through active-block and full-canvas or passive recorders.
issues.verification_test: The factorial estimates separately report boundary location and magnitude under matched allocations, while the dual-recorder comparison changes only the observation window and quantifies whether the selected periodicity persists.
issues.evidence_needed: Completed A31-X3 and A31-X4 runs with frozen protocols, per-arm raw summaries, uncertainty or randomization analyses, and artifact hashes.

issues.location: Reproducibility statement on page 9; Appendix A.3 Table 9 on page 13; Appendix B on page 18; evidence/claim_evidence_map.tsv, evidence/method_provenance.tsv, evidence/experiment_registry.json, and evidence/repository_inventory.md
issues.observed_evidence: All central claims are labeled source_reported/cannot_verify_locally; all primary experiments are reported_not_rerun; the event logs, result JSON files, and analysis code are absent; and the private checkpoint is not byte-identical to the public model. Table 9 supplies paths and short hashes but not the target artifacts. Manifest hashes for the supplied snapshot files are internally consistent, but they do not validate the reported numerical results.
issues.why_it_matters: The selector outputs, bootstrap frequencies, permutation results, and robustness checks are the central empirical evidence. None can be independently inspected or recomputed, materially reducing confidence in soundness.
issues.required_fix: Release an anonymized bundle containing releasable event streams, exact scripts, full configuration, result files, and complete hashes. If the checkpoint cannot be released, reproduce the central effect on an accessible public checkpoint or provide a sufficiently complete event-level artifact for analysis-only reproduction.
issues.verification_test: A clean environment executes the documented analysis and reproduces every central table value and selected period from the released event data; an independent checker verifies all registered hashes and arm/question assignments.
issues.evidence_needed: The missing event, script, result, manifest, and ledger artifacts identified in the repository inventory, plus either an accessible checkpoint or a public-checkpoint replication.

issues.location: Sections 2 and 3.1-3.2, Tables 2-5 on pages 3-7; Appendix A.5 and Table 10 on page 14; evidence/experiment_registry.json entry A31-X5
issues.observed_evidence: The paper explicitly states that bootstrap modal selection is not false-positive control. The original gate flagged 10/25 wrong candidates, the corrected comparison still does not calibrate the full selection procedure, L24 has pmargin=0.071, L48 rests on one boundary locus, and A31-X5 is not_run.
issues.why_it_matters: These disclosures are commendable, but they leave unclear how surprising the observed P*=L pattern is under realistic structured nulls induced by the same schedule and extremum selector. This prevents the empirical result from supporting detection or broad significance.
issues.required_fix: Run an arm-level structured null that preserves relevant dependence and schedule geometry, calibrate the complete candidate-selection procedure with family-wise control, and add independent boundary support for low-cardinality probe arms or narrow those conclusions further.
issues.verification_test: The frozen full selector has controlled family-wise error under the structured null, reports calibrated power for effect sizes observed in each arm, and the L48 conclusion no longer depends on a single boundary locus.
issues.evidence_needed: Completed A31-X5 outputs, null-generation justification, family-wise calibration, power curves, and additional probe data with multiple independent boundaries.

issues.location: Section 5 on pages 8-9; Appendix A.9 on pages 16-17; overall PDF layout, especially pages 6 and 12
issues.observed_evidence: The main related-work discussion is brief while two dense appendix tables carry the novelty argument. Several definitions and caveats recur across the main text, Appendices A.4/A.6, and Appendix C. Pages 6 and 12 contain unusually large unused regions, while other pages are table-dense.
issues.why_it_matters: Readers must work hard to identify the single novel methodological claim and distinguish it from prudent but familiar measurement practice.
issues.required_fix: Condense repeated terminology and caveats, move a short verified closest-work matrix into the main text, state the unique contribution in one falsifiable sentence, and rebalance table placement.
issues.verification_test: A reader can recover the problem, nearest prior approach, exact novelty axis, strongest evidence, and claim boundary from the abstract, introduction, and one main-text comparison without consulting multiple appendix crosswalks; the rebuilt PDF has no avoidable half-empty pages.
issues.evidence_needed: A revised, rendered manuscript and a verified concise closest-work table.

ethics_concerns: No direct human-subject, privacy, safety, or deployment concern is apparent from the frozen submission. The material concern is research integrity and reproducibility of unavailable empirical artifacts, which is addressed under soundness rather than flagged as an ethics violation.
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by an isolated AI subagent for internal pre-submission quality control. The manuscript itself discloses AI-generated qualitative Figure 1 and AI-assisted prose and LaTeX editing in Appendix B.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A complete primary-source citation audit establishing a genuine gap relative to the nearest work on schedule-aware position diagnostics and instrumentation confounds.
An identical-trajectory active-block versus full-canvas recorder experiment that isolates the observation-window effect.
A partition-by-allocation factorial and an independent model or schedule replication.
A calibrated full-selector structured null with family-wise error control and adequate boundary cardinality.
A released anonymized event-and-analysis bundle that reproduces all central tables in a clean environment.
A demonstrated downstream diagnostic decision that changes under the proposed calibrated reporting rule.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Discovery of prior work already performing the same recorder-window and block-length intervention or articulating the same two-layer rule.
Failure of the reported table values to reproduce from released event streams and scripts.
A structured-null audit showing frequent P*=L selection without the claimed empirical phenomenon.
Dual-recorder results showing that periodicity is unchanged by the active observation window while no alternative account is identified.
Failure to replicate the selection pattern on fresh arms, additional boundaries, or an accessible checkpoint.
review_limitations: The review was restricted to the frozen snapshot and did not inspect repository history, prior reviews, author plans, or files outside the submission directory.
Primary literature was not available in the snapshot; novelty and citation-support conclusions therefore rely on the partial citation lock and are marked cannot_verify where appropriate.
Central event streams, scripts, result files, and the private checkpoint were absent, so quantitative verification was impossible.
